topics.name: GLP-1 Weight Loss Drug Market
topics.summary: Eli Lilly hit $1T market cap driven by GLP-1 drugs. The $72B market is projected to exceed $100B in weight loss revenue alone by 2034. Compounders like Hims created a 3x price drop but demand growth offsets margin compression from 80% to ~60%. Next battle is oral pill formulations. Neither Eli Lilly nor Novo has a monopoly — it is a duopoly with no winner-take-all outcome.

topics.name: AI Barnyard Market Map
topics.summary: Hosts created a barnyard-themed AI market map using NanoBanana Pro image generation. Meta=pigs at slop trough, NVIDIA=cash cow, Elon/xAI=bull in china shop, Apple=lipstick on pig, Anthropic=donkey, Google=fat cat, Perplexity=headless chicken, Chinese open source=snake in the grass, SSI=dark horse, Reddit=sitting duck, Amazon=workhorse, Karpathy=black sheep, Josh Kushner=early bird, Leopold=bird's eye view, Satya=lion's share.

topics.name: Adobe Acquiring Semrush and GEO Market
topics.summary: Adobe acquiring Semrush for $1.9B. The generative engine optimization market remains highly competitive — VCs are pitched GEO companies multiple times per week. Semrush has its own early GEO product and may enter the space more aggressively post-acquisition.

topics.name: AMD and Lisa Sue Profile
topics.summary: WSJ profile of Lisa Sue who pivoted AMD to AI in a 2022 board meeting, growing market cap from $90B to $335B. AMD secured MI450 chip deal with Oracle and OpenAI. Now sells 41% of data center CPUs. Sue predicts $1T AI chip market by 2030 and says underinvesting is more dangerous than overinvesting.

topics.name: M-Dash and AI Writing Tells
topics.summary: Joel Stein's WSJ piece defended the M-dash against AI-shaming. The M-dash has become shorthand for AI-written content. Hosts argued that antithetical parallelism ('it's not X, it's Y') is an even bigger AI tell — and it appears across all major models, not just OpenAI, suggesting it was baked in from professional writing training data.

topics.name: Luxury Real Estate — Is $200M the New $100M
topics.summary: Multiple US properties listed at $200M+ concentrated in South Florida. AI wealth boom expected to drive ultra-luxury prices higher. A Silicon Valley estate in Portola Valley sold for $56M. San Francisco's 94127 zip code now second most expensive at $2.5M median list price.

topics.name: Private Equity Control of Youth Sports
topics.summary: PE firms buying hockey rinks and banning parents from filming games, forcing subscription to proprietary recording services. The issue gained national attention when enforcement targeted U.S. Senator Chris Murphy at his child's hockey game.

topics.name: Regulatory Overreach and Climate Tech
topics.summary: Charm Industrial CEO Peter Reinhart's viral post described $27M in certification costs for their Revoi device that reduces truck emissions by 90%, with $100K per certification across 270 engine families. Cited as a systemic problem stifling clean tech innovation.

topics.name: Private Credit Distress — Cockroach Problem
topics.summary: 4840 Solutions pallet company restructuring as lenders KKR, BlackRock, Carlisle swap $1.75B debt for equity after Summit Partners' buyout. Hosts noted private credit firms increasingly converting debt to equity to prevent outright losses. Jamie Dimon's cockroach analogy referenced.

topics.name: Legibility to Capital
topics.summary: Will Minaitis long-form post argued the single greatest superpower for a firm is being magnetically legible to capital — where founder and idea are inseparable, growth is a superlinear function of dollars in, and all stakeholders share the exact same vision. Examples cited: Ramp, Cognition, Leopold, Thrive Capital.

topics.name: California Forever City Project
topics.summary: Julia Steinberg's Arena Magazine piece on the privately funded new city in Solano County backed by Lorraine Powell Jobs, Collison Brothers, Hoffman, and Andreessen. Project is stalled by a 12,000-page environmental review and other government hurdles despite private capital backing.

topics.name: Chinese Open Source AI Models
topics.summary: DeepSeek and Kimi discussed as threats to closed-source model pricing power. Hosts debated whether soft power concerns are overstated for B2B automation use cases, agreeing it is more of a business model threat than a cultural one, though application-layer proliferation globally remains a concern.

topics.name: OpenAI Headwinds from Google Gemini
topics.summary: Sam Altman publicly acknowledged temporary economic headwinds from resurgent Google. Gemini 3 Pro described as top-tier on reasoning, multimodal, and coding benchmarks. Hosts debated whether stickiness of ChatGPT brand is sufficient to maintain API and consumer dominance.

topics.name: College Admissions, Law School, and AI Labor Market
topics.summary: Julia Steinberg discussed witnessing the college admissions scandal firsthand. One third of Stanford class of 2025 co-termed. Law school applications rising despite AI automating associate work — debated whether top 5% of law students can still build strong careers or whether the track is becoming an MLM-like value trap.

topics.name: San Francisco Housing and Recovery
topics.summary: West Portal zip code now second most expensive in SF at $2.5M median list price. OpenAI secondary market wealth expected to drive real estate prices higher in a 20-mile radius. Julia Steinberg described ongoing homelessness issues in Pacific Heights despite recovery narrative.

topics.name: Dupe Shopping App and Agentic Commerce
topics.summary: Bobby Ghoshal discussed Dupe's approach to finding similar products for less using vectorized product catalogs and brand partnerships. Hit #1 in App Store on launch day. Approaching $100M GMV with 18M total shoppers. Building MCP to let LLMs plug in and split commerce commissions.
